page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r8a.16xlarge is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine instance deployed on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by dedicated AMD EPYC 9T24 processors operating at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz across 64 virtual central processing units. The instance is provisioned with 512.0 GB of system memory, establishing a consistent memory density of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is absent, with zero dedicated GPUs attached to the instance profile.

Networking performance is configured with a 20 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, supporting substantial throughput for network-intensive communications. The instance does not include bundled local storage disks, requiring external cloud block storage for persistent file systems and operating system installations. In addition, no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned directly to the instance, requiring explicit elastic IP allocation for external Internet connectivity.

In terms of resource architecture and cost efficiency, the ecs.r8a.16xlarge delivers high compute and RAM allocation per host footprint, matching the requirements of large-footprint enterprise services. The absence of integrated local NVMe storage reduces overhead for systems architected around disaggregated storage layers, though it necessitates consideration of remote disk latency. The instance is structured for memory-heavy workloads, including large-scale in-memory databases, Redis caching clusters, high-throughput ETL processing, and enterprise data analytics.

It incorporates a 20 Gbps baseline network interface to sustain heavy cluster traffic. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage or dedicated graphics processing units, operating entirely with remote network-attached block devices for root and data volumes. It also includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. With its high memory-to-core ratio and dedicated multi-core capacity, ecs.r8a.16xlarge is structured for memory-intensive enterprise software, including distributed caching tiers, in-memory relational and non-relational database management systems, and large-scale data analytics pipelines.
